title: Ten questions about your mood
body: The next ten questions are the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. They ask how you have felt in the past seven days. This is not a diagnosis. It is one set of answers your care team can use. Your answers go to: {{shared_with}}. You can skip this step.

title: Nine questions about your mood
body: The next nine questions are the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. They ask how often things have bothered you in the past two weeks. This is not a diagnosis. It is one set of answers your care team can use. Your answers go to: {{shared_with}}. You can skip this step.

title: A few questions about how you are
body: These questions ask how you have felt in the past seven days. Grief is not an illness, and this is not a diagnosis. Your care team uses your answers to decide what support to offer. Your answers go to: {{shared_with}}. You can skip this step, now or every time.

title: One answer is always shared
body: If you answer yes to the question about harming yourself, your care team will be told even if you chose nobody yet.

title: What stays private
body: If you answer yes to the question about harming yourself, your care team will not be told if you chose nobody yet. You will see the emergency instruction and the crisis line instead.

title: A short set of mood questions
body: You said things are hard right now. A short set of mood questions can help your care team know what to offer. You can answer now or at your next check-in. You can also say no.

title: Who should see these answers?
body: Last time you chose nobody yet. Do you want to share these answers with your care team this time? One tap. You can keep nobody yet.
